diagram.manim_description: Canvas 16:9, plain BG white, 16 units wide by 9 units high with 1 unit = 120 px at 1920 px wide; origin at the top-left corner, x grows to the right, y grows downward. Draw two vertical chains of four equations each. The left chain is centred on x = 4.3 and the right chain on x = 12.3. The four equation rows are centred on y = 1.2, 3.4, 5.6 and 7.8. Every equation is INK, 52 px, centred on its chain's x, variables in italic. Left chain, row 1 to row 4: 'y + 1 = 6', '−y − 1 = −6', '−1 = −6 + y', '5 = y'. Right chain, row 1 to row 4: '3y = 15', '3y + 6 = 21', 'y + 2 = 7', 'y = 5'. Between each two consecutive equations of a chain draw one downward single-headed INK arrow with a 3 px stroke at x = chain x + 0.2, running from 0.45 units below the centre of the upper equation to 0.45 units above the centre of the lower equation. Write its operation label in INK, 38 px, with the label's left edge at x = chain x + 0.5, centred vertically on the gap between the two rows (y = upper row + 1.1). Left chain labels, top gap to bottom gap: 'Multiplying by −1', 'Adding y', 'Adding 6'. Right chain labels, top gap to bottom gap: 'Adding 6', 'Dividing by 3', 'Subtracting 2'. Draw nothing else: no frame, no upward arrow, no heading and no fill colour.
must_not_show: any upward arrow or upward operation label
the words Chain 1 or Chain 2 or any other heading
the value of y written beside any equation
accuracy_checks: 8 equations: 4 per chain, left chain rows read y + 1 = 6, −y − 1 = −6, −1 = −6 + y, 5 = y; right chain rows read 3y = 15, 3y + 6 = 21, y + 2 = 7, y = 5
6 downward arrows (3 per chain) with labels exactly as printed on book p.17 (Multiplying by −1, Adding y, Adding 6 / Adding 6, Dividing by 3, Subtracting 2)

each downward operation turns the equation above it into the equation below it (×−1 on y + 1 = 6 gives −y − 1 = −6; +y gives −1 = −6 + y; +6 gives 5 = y; +6 on 3y = 15 gives 3y + 6 = 21; ÷3 gives y + 2 = 7; −2 gives y = 5)
diagram.alt_text: Two chains of equations read top to bottom with a downward arrow and its operation between each pair: y + 1 = 6, −y − 1 = −6, −1 = −6 + y, 5 = y; and 3y = 15, 3y + 6 = 21, y + 2 = 7, y = 5.
diagram.render_note: Same picture as book p.17 and as the teaching image M3.S20.T20.C120.IMG1 (which is not linked); labels use the book's wording (Multiplying by, Adding, Dividing by, Subtracting). Equations as printed in the book, including −y − 1 = −6.
